subject: economics
title: Boardroom Exam Stretch
welcome_lead: You're a strategy consultant. Evaluate automation, productivity investment and the human cost of change.
meta_desc: GCSE Economics exam-style adventure on production: evaluation of automation, training and productivity policy.
final_note: Production strategy mastered. Banking and finance next!

concepts.def: Falling unit cost as output rises.
Workers/firms focus on a narrow task.

walkthroughs.body_html: 1) Capital investment — better machines. 2) Training — better human capital. 3) Better management — Toyota-style lean processes. Each has costs and time-lags. Top-band answers weigh ROI vs upfront costs.

Robots cut unit costs and raise quality but displace low-skill workers (structural unemployment). Long term, new jobs emerge in design and maintenance. Evaluation: depends on retraining, region, speed of change.
Use: time lag, cost, magnitude, distributional impact, and opportunity cost. Conclude with a justified judgement: which policy is most effective and why, in this context.

mcqs.q: Which is most likely to RAISE UK productivity in the long run?
options: Investing in worker skills and new tech
